input:
It should be reported that a budget overrun of 4 weeks has now built up on the current package, the cause of which is the late completion of the EPC scope that feeds into the package: work which ought to have been closed out before the package got under way has instead continued to run alongside it, with the result that the package has effectively carried both its own costs and the costs of the unfinished work within the same accounts. It should also be noted that the overrun is by no means spread evenly across the package as a whole; it is concentrated in that part of the work which depends on the unfinished scope, while the remainder of the package continues to run at its planned rate.

The mitigation that is proposed in response to this position is that outstanding commitments on the package should be re-approved before they are placed, in order to ensure that no further cost is committed against the package until each commitment has been properly checked against the state of the scope that it serves. Responsibility for this mitigation sits with the project board, which will hold the re-approval process, and any work that cannot pass through that process will be held rather than being charged on in the expectation that the position will in due course correct itself.

The overrun is not spread evenly across the package; it sits in the part of the work that depends on the unfinished scope, and the remainder of the package is running at its planned rate. The position is reported as it stands, without allowance for recovery that has not yet been earned.

The mitigation proposed is that outstanding commitments on the package are re-approved before they are placed, so that no further cost is committed against the package until the commitment has been checked against the state of the scope it serves. Responsibility for the mitigation sits with the project board: the board holds the re-approval, and work that cannot pass it is held rather than charged on in the expectation that the position will correct itself.
